To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the immediate recovery of replication after UV‐induced inhibition in Escherichia coil requires pol II and the PriA protein; (2) pol V‐dependent replication readthrough is delayed by 50 min and occurs after pol II‐dependent replication has been completed; (3) RecF, O, and R are important factors for the formation of Rec‐dependent recombination structures that are required for the PriA‐polII‐dependent replication restart; (4) Rec

pol II and the PriA‐dependent primosome‐forming function are essential for the rapid resumption of replication after UV irradiation, whereas pol V‐mediated translesion replication occurs only after a delay and requires the RecF, O, R and recA730 proteins.

pol II and the PriA‐dependent origin‐independent replication primosome are essential for immediate restart, whereas pol V‐dependent replication readthrough is a slower pathway that occurs only after the immediate restart has failed and requires RecF but not RecO or RecR for its activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of several proteins involved in replication restart in Escherichia‐coli after UV‐induced replication arrest.
the mechanism of DNA replication restart and how it is coordinated with other cellular processes.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the recovery from replication arrest and the restart of replication in UV‐iradiated Escherichiocoli.
